seoTitle: How to Use Trello's Timeline View
metaDescription: Switch a Trello board into Timeline view to see cards laid out on a date grid by list, member, or label, and schedule unscheduled cards with a click.
intro: A standard Trello board is great for tracking what state something is in, but it doesn't tell you much about when things are happening. Switching to Timeline view fixes that: instead of columns for stages, you get a date grid with each card shown as a bar across the days it covers, grouped however you like. This guide walks through what that view looks like on a real board, how to move through different time periods, and how to get an unscheduled card onto the calendar in the first place.
costNote: Timeline view is limited to Trello boards and Workspaces on Premium or Enterprise. Trello's own documentation says there are no current plans to bring it to free Workspaces, so there's no free equivalent to switch to instead.

steps.heading: Start from the regular board
steps.body: Before switching views, it helps to know what you're working from: a normal Kanban board with lists like Useful Stuff, Planned: September, Draft, Pending Editing, and Published, each holding a handful of cards. The view switcher sits alongside this same board, so nothing about your lists or cards changes when you switch. You're looking at the same data laid out differently.

image.caption: A Trello board in its normal list layout, with Board selected at the bottom next to Inbox and Planner.

steps.heading: Switch to Timeline view
steps.body: From the board, open the view switcher and choose Timeline. At the top you'll see the current month and year, Today and arrow buttons for moving between periods, and two dropdowns: one for the time range shown (Week, in this case, though Trello also offers Day, Month, Quarter, and Year), and one for how cards are grouped, set here to List. The other grouping options are Member, Label, or None, so a team can switch from "what's scheduled per list" to "what's scheduled per person" without leaving the view. Down the left side, each of your board's lists appears as its own row, with a count of how many of its cards aren't yet scheduled.

image.caption: Timeline view for June 2026, grouped by List, with each list showing how many of its cards have no date yet.

steps.heading: Read the grid and the unscheduled counts
steps.body: Every row is a list from your board (or a member or label, if you've regrouped); every column is a day. A card with a start and due date shows up as a bar spanning the days it covers, but a fresh board or template mostly has cards sitting in "Not scheduled" until you actively place them, which is exactly what the small blue count next to each row is telling you. That count is worth checking before you assume the timeline is complete; an empty-looking grid usually just means nothing has a date yet, not that nothing is planned.

steps.heading: Schedule an unscheduled card
steps.body: Click the "+" next to a row's "Not scheduled" count to open an overview of that row's unscheduled cards, then click one to assign it a due date. Once a card has a date and appears as a bar, you can also click and hold its edge to stretch it, setting or adjusting a start and end date directly on the grid instead of reopening the card. Working through a list a few cards at a time beats trying to plan the whole board in one sitting.

steps.heading: Move between months to see further out
steps.body: The arrow buttons next to Today step you forward and back one period at a time, and the label at top-left updates to match. The same board can show June 2026 one moment and December 2024 the next, useful for checking whether older due dates were ever set correctly or for planning several months ahead in one pass.

image.caption: The same Timeline view navigated back to December 2024, with the scheduling panel still open for the Useful Stuff list.

steps.heading: Switch the grouping or time range as needed
steps.body: The grouping dropdown moves between List, Member, Label, or None, and the range dropdown moves between Day, Week, Month, Quarter, and Year. Try a wider range first to get a sense of the overall spread of dated versus undated cards, then narrow to Week or Day once you're scheduling specific cards, since a tight view makes it easier to avoid double-booking a date by accident.

troubleshooting.problem: Timeline doesn't show up in the view switcher at all
troubleshooting.cause: Timeline view only ships on Trello Premium and Enterprise. Trello has stated it has no plans to extend it to free Workspaces.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your Workspace's plan under billing settings. If you're on Premium or Enterprise and it's still missing, confirm you're looking at a board-level view switcher, not a Workspace-level one.

troubleshooting.problem: The board looks almost empty in Timeline view
troubleshooting.cause: Cards without a start or due date don't get a bar. They sit in that row's "Not scheduled" count until given a date.
troubleshooting.fix: Click the "+" next to Not scheduled for the row in question to open the overview and assign dates to those cards.

faq.question: Do I need a paid plan to use Timeline view?
faq.answer: Yes. Timeline view is limited to Trello Premium and Enterprise Workspaces, and Trello has said it has no current plans to bring it to the free tier.

faq.question: What's the difference between Timeline view and Calendar view?
faq.answer: Both need Premium or Enterprise. Calendar view is a simple week or month grid of due dates with no grouping. Timeline view adds grouping by list, member, or label, plus Day/Week/Month/Quarter/Year ranges, so it can show a second dimension alongside dates.

faq.question: What does the count next to each row mean?
faq.answer: It shows how many cards in that list, member, or label group don't have a scheduled date yet. A board can look empty in Timeline view simply because most cards haven't been dated.

faq.question: How do I put an undated card onto the timeline?
faq.answer: Click the "+" next to that row's Not scheduled count. A panel opens listing the unscheduled cards so you can assign one a date directly.

faq.question: Can I look at past months, not just upcoming ones?
faq.answer: Yes. The arrow buttons next to Today move the view backward and forward through any period, and Today jumps straight back to the current date.

faq.question: Can I change how cards are grouped?
faq.answer: Yes. The grouping dropdown switches between List, Member, Label, or None, letting you see the same dated cards organized by person or tag instead of by list.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in July 2025. Re-checked against Atlassian's official Timeline view and Calendar view documentation in September 2026. That check corrected the plan requirement from a vague "generally part of Trello's paid plans" to the documented Premium/Enterprise-only gate, named the grouping options (List, Member, Label, None) and full time-range list (Day, Week, Month, Quarter, Year) that the previous version only partly described, and added the card-stretching mechanic for setting date ranges directly on the grid.
